errors: First commit's post description was 183 characters (limit 160); caught locally by run_workflow_locally.py before CI, fixed in a follow-up commit.

doc_friction.issue: Step 3 says rerun sets caught_after_fix on every escaped mutant, but it skips mutants triaged equivalent (caught_after_fix stays null), so checking an equivalence claim against the new tests means re-applying the mutant by hand. One line saying so would save the confusion.

Step 0's open list was 5 entries, all already covered by open control-plane PRs awaiting the owner; redteam.py open does not show that, so each run re-checks the PR list. Linking the PR in the entry (patched_in: pending #N) would make the list read as handled.

deviations.why: Step 4b prefers a CI-level guard; the defect class here (two twins drifting) is venture-local, so the guard is a parity corpus in the venture's own suite, which ventures-tests.yml already runs on every PR.
deviations.did: Added parity-cases.test.json + a parity test in classify.test.mjs instead of a platform/ci lint.
deviations.result: Fails when the fix is reverted in one twin only; runs in CI with no workflow change.

goal: Measure how many seeded faults the systemd-unit-hardening-check suites catch, hunt real defects, patch and guard them.
notes: Target chosen because it is a security checker that landed on main this week (#14794) with a Python CLI and a JS browser twin. Campaigns: check.py 8 mutants (5 caught), classify.mjs 10 (8 caught). Hunt: differential run of 57 hostile unit files through both twins (all agreed) then read against systemd.exec(5): DynamicUser=yes + User=root was not flagged as root. Guard added: parity-cases.test.json edge-case corpus run through both twins in classify.test.mjs; verified it fails when the fix is reverted in the JS twin only. Verification: python3 -m unittest test_check (19 OK), node --test classify/page/usage (25 pass), run_venture_tests.py systemd-unit-hardening-check ok, run_workflow_locally.py --for-changes: portfolio-validate 100/100, ventures-tests 5/5 and the rest green; it caught the new post's description at 183 chars (limit 160: hub tests and check_post_frontmatter.py), fixed in a second commit; the remaining local failures were the skipped site build (no _site/dist) and the 300 s budget. PR CI on the fixed head: all 20 check runs success or skipped.

mutants.note: A doubled trailing backslash at EOF leaves one backslash inside an open quote; the mutant reads value[k+1] past the end and crashes the whole scan (IndexError). test_unterminated_quote_ending_in_backslash.

mutants.note: The JS twin appends 'undefined' instead of nothing for a trailing backslash in an open quote, but the parsed value only feeds the empty / %d / /run/credentials / boolean predicates, and the finding text names the variable, never its value, so no output changes; envAssignments is not exported. Re-applied by hand after the new tests: all 9 classify.test.mjs tests (including the edge-case parity corpus, which has this input) still pass, consistent with equivalence.

mutants.before: const cmp = (a, b) => (a < b ? -1 : a > b ? 1 : 0);
mutants.after: const cmp = (a, b) => (a < b ? -1 : a > b ? 2 : 0);
mutants.line_text: const cmp = (a, b) => (a < b ? -1 : a > b ? 1 : 0);
mutants.note: cmp returns 2 instead of 1 for a > b; Array.prototype.sort only uses the sign, so the drop-in order is identical.

real_defects.issue: DynamicUser=yes with User=root (or User=0) got no svc-runs-as-root finding in check.py or classify.mjs, though systemd.exec(5) says a static user of the configured name is used instead of a dynamic one (root always exists) and the README's own rule table says User=root is flagged. Fixed in both twins with failing tests first; an edge-case parity corpus (57 hostile units) now keeps the Python CLI and the browser classifier in lockstep.

certainty.api_equivalent_usd: medium: measured tokens x list prices in prompts/pricing.json (as_of stated); an equivalent, not a charge: these runs are billed under a subscription
certainty.time: medium: from transcript timestamps; model time is request-to-response, tool time is call-to-result, time waiting on a person is excluded from active time
certainty.human_equivalent: low: the agent's own estimate of how long a competent person would take, with its basis written down; never measured
